rows.under: Closes the method because it just worked.
rows.justRight: Asks one person who does it differently what they would change, and tries the part that fits.
rows.over: Abandons a working method at the first alternative.

rows.under: Confuses confidence with arrogance and still needs a decision.
rows.justRight: Decides, and holds the decision lightly enough to update when the evidence changes.
rows.over: Refuses to decide because any choice might look proud.

rows.situation: A teammate stuck on other work
rows.under: Leaves them stuck because it is not your goal.
rows.justRight: Spends a bounded slice of time to unblock them, then returns to your own commitment.
rows.over: Takes over their goal and drops the result you owed.

rows.under: Waits for the official owner, who is not around, while the person stays blocked.
rows.justRight: Answers what you know, says what you do not, and points at the owner for the rest.
rows.over: Answers beyond what you know and sends them down the wrong path with confidence.

rows.under: Keeps a task that someone else needs to touch, because sharing it would slow you today.
rows.justRight: Shares the context and lets them do the part that is theirs, even if you could finish it faster.
rows.over: Hands off work you have not explained, and calls the dump collaboration.

rows.situation: Help that was not asked for
rows.under: Watches them struggle because they did not ask in the right way.
rows.justRight: Offers once, specifically, and accepts a no.
rows.over: Helps over the refusal and rewrites their work.

rows.under: Helps everyone else and surprises your stakeholders when your goal slips.
rows.justRight: Helps in a way that still lets you warn early if your own date moves.
rows.over: Refuses every request the moment your own date looks tight, including a ten-minute unblock.

rows.situation: Work that crosses into your area
rows.under: Treats their edit as an intrusion.
rows.justRight: Welcomes the useful change, reviews it, and keeps ownership of the outcome.
rows.over: Lets anyone edit anything so you never have to say no, and the result has no owner.

rows.under: Takes the shortcut and leaves the cost with every other team.
rows.justRight: Takes it only if the total time and energy go down, and says who pays if they do not.
rows.over: Bans the shortcut even when it is cheaper for everyone, because it was not invented centrally.

rows.under: Builds a tool that saves your team an hour and costs the community a day of exceptions.
rows.justRight: Uses the shared path, or fixes the shared path, instead of a private one.
rows.over: Forces a global tool that is worse than the local one for every team, including yours.

rows.under: Special-cases one person's workflow and everyone else routes around it.
rows.justRight: Asks whether the change helps the broader group, and declines it when it does not.
rows.over: Refuses a one-person fix that would also remove a trap for everyone else.

rows.under: Saves money and spends a week of people's time to do it, or the reverse, without counting.
rows.justRight: Counts the scarce thing, including time and energy, and picks the cheaper total.
rows.over: Optimizes a spreadsheet while the actual waste is in the work.

rows.under: Rebuilds a novel version because the shared one is dull.
rows.justRight: Uses the boring shared solution and improves it where it fails the broader group.
rows.over: Standardizes on a boring solution that does not do the job, and forbids the fix.

rows.under: Celebrates a local saving that moved the cost one team over.
rows.justRight: Reports the effect on the whole path, not only on your step.
rows.over: Ignores a real local waste because you cannot prove the global number today.

rows.under: Lets the usual voices run the meeting and reads silence as comfort.
rows.justRight: Notices who has not spoken, asks for that view, and makes it safe to give it.
rows.over: Calls on people to represent a category, which puts them on the spot instead of in the work.

rows.situation: A norm that fits one kind of life
rows.under: Sets the hours, the social plan, or the ritual around the people who already fit it.
rows.justRight: Changes the one norm that keeps a teammate from contributing, and keeps the bar on the work.
rows.over: Drops the work expectation so the norm never has to be discussed.

rows.situation: A room that all looks the same
rows.under: Does not notice, or notices and does nothing about how the next person gets in.
rows.justRight: Changes how you source and assess the next seat so the room can include someone the current pattern misses.
rows.over: Hires for the appearance of variety and does not give the person real work.

rows.under: Plans the event around one kind of body, budget, or family situation.
rows.justRight: Asks what would keep people out and changes that part before the invitations go.
rows.over: Cancels every gathering so there is no risk of excluding anyone, and the team never meets.

rows.under: Puts the words on a page and leaves the meeting unchanged.
rows.justRight: Picks one behavior in the week's meetings that will be different, and checks whether it was.
rows.over: Builds a campaign about belonging while the person being talked about is not in the work.

rows.under: Withholds a hard assignment so a person never has to struggle in public.
rows.justRight: Gives the hard assignment with the support to succeed, because contribution is what belonging is for.
rows.over: Uses the assignment as a test they are expected to fail.

rows.situation: A big change that could be a slice
rows.under: Builds the whole thing before anyone uses it.
rows.justRight: Ships the smallest slice that a real user can complete, and learns from that.
rows.over: Ships a slice so thin that the user cannot do the job, and calls the confusion learning.

rows.situation: Feedback from the people who use it
rows.under: Asks the team what they think and never asks a user.
rows.justRight: Puts the slice in front of a user, or uses it yourself as they would, and changes the next slice.
rows.over: Rewrites the slice after every comment, including comments that do not bear on the goal.

rows.under: Breaks the path people already rely on so the iteration can move faster.
rows.justRight: Keeps the current path working and adds the slice beside it until the new one is ready.
rows.over: Preserves every old path forever and the iteration never replaces anything.

rows.under: Starts the next slice before you know whether this one worked.
rows.justRight: Names what would prove the slice worked, checks that, and only then continues.
rows.over: Demands statistical certainty from a handful of uses and stalls.

rows.under: Polishes an internal detail and calls it an iteration.
rows.justRight: Chooses a step that answers a real question about the end goal.
rows.over: Makes the step so large that the feedback arrives after the design is frozen.

rows.under: Ships to users a thing the team has not tried to use.
rows.justRight: Uses it for a real task first, fixes the break you hit, and then asks others.
rows.over: Refuses to show users anything until the team is fully satisfied with it.

rows.situation: A decision in a private chat
rows.under: Leaves the decision in the private thread and wonders why others redo it.
rows.justRight: Moves the decision to a place the people who need it can read, and links the reason.
rows.over: Pastes a private conversation, including asides that were never meant to be shared.

rows.situation: A project only the team can see
rows.under: Defaults to a private project because that is easier.
rows.justRight: Makes it public unless there is a concrete reason not to, and writes that reason down.
rows.over: Makes public a project that contains customer data or a personnel matter.

rows.under: Asks for contributions and keeps the context in your head.
rows.justRight: Publishes the goal, the status, and how to propose a change.
rows.over: Publishes so much unfinished noise that contributing is harder than asking you.

rows.situation: A real reason to stay private
rows.under: Uses privacy as the habit, not as a reason.
rows.justRight: Keeps private what would hurt a customer, a person, or an unannounced commitment, and makes the rest public.
rows.over: Announces that everything is public and then hides the actual decision anyway.

rows.under: Files it where only your team will see it.
rows.justRight: Files it in the public tracker with enough detail that someone outside the team could help.
rows.over: Files a vague public issue and then ignores the people who show up.

rows.under: Leaves a public doc you know is stale because correcting it is awkward.
rows.justRight: Corrects it in public and says what changed.
rows.over: Deletes the history so the mistake is harder to see than the fix.

rows.under: Talks about the other site, team, or project as the obstacle.
rows.justRight: Names the shared goal and the specific handoff, and drops the us-and-them wording.
rows.over: Polices other people's wording and never fixes the handoff.

rows.under: Keeps it inside the team because they did not ask yet.
rows.justRight: Sends it to the people who will trip on it, before they trip.
rows.over: Broadcasts every detail to every group and the signal disappears.

rows.situation: Asking when you do not know
rows.under: Guesses, or waits, because asking would cross a boundary.
rows.justRight: Asks the person who knows, wherever they sit, and shares the answer back.
rows.over: Asks so many groups that you create a second project out of the question.

rows.situation: A silo that formed on its own
rows.under: Treats the silo as inevitable and routes around it.
rows.justRight: Puts one regular touch in place with the other group and uses it for a real decision.
rows.over: Dissolves every working group in the name of unity, and the work loses its owners.

rows.situation: A win told as only yours
rows.under: Reports the win as your team's, and leaves out the group that made it possible.
rows.justRight: Reports it as a shared result and says what each side did.
rows.over: Refuses to name any team, so nobody knows who to ask next time.

rows.under: Celebrates your date and ignores that the other group will miss theirs because of you.
rows.justRight: Moves your date, or your scope, when that is what keeps the joint outcome intact.
rows.over: Holds your work until every other group is ready, including groups this release does not need.

rows.under: Misses it and lets people find out when the work is not there.
rows.justRight: Tells them as soon as you know, with the new date you can actually hold.
rows.over: Sends daily warnings before you know anything, and they stop reading them.

rows.under: Leaves the goal undated because the date would be uncomfortable.
rows.justRight: Puts a date on it, or a date for when the date will be set, and writes it where stakeholders look.
rows.over: Invents a date you have no plan to hit, so the surprise is merely delayed.

rows.under: Waits for the date itself, hoping you will recover.
rows.justRight: Says it the day you know, including what will still arrive and what will not.
rows.over: Declares a slip at the first hard day, before you know whether the date is actually lost.

rows.under: Saves the bad news for the meeting so you can explain it live.
rows.justRight: Sends the news before the meeting, and uses the meeting to decide what to do.
rows.over: Sends a flood of minor updates so the one real surprise is harder to see.

rows.under: Says you will know later and does not say when.
rows.justRight: Commits to the day you will either give the date or explain what is still unknown.
rows.over: Schedules a meeting to schedule the meeting, and calls that a date.

rows.under: Quietly redefines done so the original date looks met.
rows.justRight: Delivers what you named, or renegotiates the meaning of done before the date, not after.
rows.over: Hits the date by handing over something the other person cannot use, with no warning.

rows.situation: A meeting that could be a note
rows.under: Holds the meeting because it is on the calendar.
rows.justRight: Sends the note, asks for the decision in writing, and cancels the meeting.
rows.over: Refuses every meeting, including the one where a decision actually requires the room.

rows.situation: A message that wastes the reader
rows.under: Sends a brain dump and lets three people hunt for the ask.
rows.justRight: Puts the ask, the deadline, and the context they need in the first lines.
rows.over: Over-edits a two-line ask for an hour and the decision window closes.

rows.under: Saves the money and spends a week of people on a problem a purchase would remove.
rows.justRight: Spends the money when the time it gives back is the scarcer resource, and says why.
rows.over: Spends freely and calls every purchase a time saving, including ones that create more work.

rows.under: Schedules the second week as if the first had no cost.
rows.justRight: Treats the second week as exceptional, cuts scope, and puts recovery time on the calendar.
rows.over: Bans any extra hour even when a one-time push would prevent a larger mess.

rows.under: Drops by, calls, and forwards threads before you have made the question clear.
rows.justRight: Does the thinking first, then asks for the smallest slice of their time that you still need.
rows.over: Will not ask at all, and burns your own week on something they could have answered.

rows.situation: Recovery as part of the work
rows.under: Praises the person who skipped recovery and quietly expects the same.
rows.justRight: Plans the recovery when you plan the overtime, and does not treat it as a favor.
rows.over: Protects recovery by slipping a commitment you could have reduced in scope instead.

rows.situation: A cheap version that does not work
rows.under: Ships the lean version and leaves the user with a result that is not fit for the job.
rows.justRight: Spends what the job actually requires, and nothing past that.
rows.over: Rebuilds it lavishly because the first version was embarrassing, past the point of fit.

rows.under: Adds finish the job does not need because the lean version feels exposed.
rows.justRight: Stops when it is fit for purpose and writes down what you refused to add.
rows.over: Calls every finish waste, including the one a user needs to complete the task.

rows.under: Picks lean or polished and does not say what you gave up.
rows.justRight: Says what fit for purpose requires here, and what you are leaving out on purpose.
rows.over: Debates the philosophy and does not decide the scope.

rows.under: Keeps refining after it already does the job and nothing more is needed.
rows.justRight: Does one more pass only for a gap a real user would hit, then stops.
rows.over: Stops at the first draft and calls the gaps a style.

rows.under: Saves the effort and hands the user the sharp edge.
rows.justRight: Spends the effort on the edge the user touches, and stays lean everywhere else.
rows.over: Pads every edge and the work is no longer lean or late.

rows.under: Reuses a scrappy shortcut in a place where the purpose is unforgiving.
rows.justRight: Matches the effort to this purpose, which may mean more care than the last job needed.
rows.over: Applies the most careful standard from the last job to a throwaway experiment.

rows.under: Falls in love with the method and does not check whether the customer can feel the result.
rows.justRight: Uses the method only as far as it makes the product better, and stops there.
rows.over: Drops a method that is working because it is not interesting anymore.

rows.under: Extends the study after it has already answered the product question.
rows.justRight: Ends the study when the product decision is clear, and writes down the decision.
rows.over: Skips the study and guesses, then calls the guess customer love.

rows.under: Spends the review on the technique and never asks what the user will do.
rows.justRight: Starts from the user's job and lets the method defend itself only where it changes that job.
rows.over: Bans the method because it looks like research, even where it is the right tool.

rows.situation: Science in service of the product
rows.under: Treats rigor as a distraction from shipping.
rows.justRight: Uses the rigor to choose a design the customer will love, then ships that design.
rows.over: Ships the research notes instead of the product change.

rows.situation: Keeping the customer in the room
rows.under: Debates the model after the customer's pain is already obvious.
rows.justRight: Names the customer pain, then picks the smallest rigorous step that would address it.
rows.over: Quotes the customer and skips the thinking that would turn the quote into a product.

rows.situation: A shortcut that hurts the product
rows.under: Takes a sloppy shortcut and hopes the customer will not notice.
rows.justRight: Takes a shortcut only if the product the customer touches still holds up.
rows.over: Refuses every shortcut, including one that would get a better product to them sooner.

rows.under: Wraps an experiment in the full release process and learns nothing this month.
rows.justRight: Uses a light process, labels the work as early, and keeps it away from the certified path.
rows.over: Treats the experiment as if a failure would be harmless in the certified system.

rows.situation: A certified change treated as a sketch
rows.under: Edits a certified system with the habits of a prototype.
rows.justRight: Uses the checks that system requires, and does not borrow speed from the research bench.
rows.over: Adds research-grade ceremony on top of the certified checks and misses the real gate.

rows.under: Uses whichever habit you used last, regardless of which world this task is in.
rows.justRight: Says which world this task is in before you start, and switches habits on purpose.
rows.over: Writes a new process for the switch and spends the week on the process.

rows.situation: A process from the wrong world
rows.under: Copies the certified checklist into the lab, or the lab's shortcuts into the certified line.
rows.justRight: Keeps a short list of what differs, and follows the list for this task.
rows.over: Maintains two full process empires and makes people serve the process instead of the work.

rows.under: Applies one rigor to every task because it is simpler to remember.
rows.justRight: Raises the rigor when the harm of being wrong goes up, and lowers it when you are still learning.
rows.over: Argues about the classification for longer than the task would have taken.

rows.under: Reports an experiment and a certified result in the same breath, as if they were the same kind of evidence.
rows.justRight: Labels which is which, every time, including in the summary a leader will skim.
rows.over: Separates them so aggressively that a lesson from the lab is not allowed to inform the product.

rows.under: Chooses the finalist with the same background and the same way of thinking. The finalist who would do the job better does not get the offer.
rows.justRight: Chooses the finalist who will do this role best, and says which parts of the work decided it.
rows.over: Chooses the weaker finalist so the team will look more varied on paper.

rows.under: Treats a shared background and the same skills as proof they can do the job. The interviews never test the work.
rows.justRight: Tests the work. A shared background is not a reason to hire them, and it is not a reason to pass.
rows.over: Rejects them for sharing that background, even though they are the best person for the role.

rows.situation: A gap in the first month
rows.under: Waves off a real gap because the candidate will be easy to manage. The team finds the gap after the offer.
rows.justRight: Names the gap, asks whether this person is still the best choice for the role, and hires only if the answer is yes.
rows.over: Hires them with the gap because a target says the next person should change how the team looks. Other people then do the work the role was opened to do.

rows.under: Asks only people who share the hiring manager's background, thinking style, and skills to do the interviews. Every vote repeats the same narrow judgment.
rows.justRight: Asks people who can test the role, including someone whose skills differ, and still decides on who can do the job.
rows.over: Picks interviewers so the panel will hit a target for who should be in the room. A strong candidate gets a no, and the work was never the question.

rows.situation: A referral from your own circle
rows.under: Moves the referral ahead because they come from the same places and think the same way. Someone who might do the job better waits.
rows.justRight: Runs the same bar as any other candidate. The referral gets the offer only if they are the best person for the role.
rows.over: Sets aside a strong referral so the team will not look narrower, and offers the role to someone less able to do it.

rows.under: Writes the role as a copy of the manager: the same background and the same skills. People who could do the work better never match the posting.
rows.justRight: Writes the work the role must do, then hires the best person who can do that work.
rows.over: Writes the role as a slot in a target for how the team should look. The posting describes the look, not the work.

rows.under: Builds a team with the same background, the same thinking style, and the same skills as the manager. The same blind spots show up in every review, and nobody in the room catches them.
rows.justRight: Hires the best person for each role, and chooses backgrounds, styles, and skills because that mix makes the business outcome better.
rows.over: Sets a target for how the team should look and accepts a weaker hire to hit it. The team under-delivers because it was not built for the outcome.

rows.under: Hires again from the same background and the same skills after the team misses the same kind of problem. The next person would have missed it too.
rows.justRight: Names the judgment or the skill the team lacks, then hires the best person who can close that gap and still do the role.
rows.over: Adds someone who changes how the team looks on paper and does not have the missing skill. The miss happens again.

rows.under: Hires people who decide the way the manager decides. A bad call gets no pushback until a customer feels it.
rows.justRight: Includes styles that challenge the default, because the outcome is better when the room is not one temperament.
rows.over: Collects contrasting styles to hit a target for how the room looks. The meeting never reaches the decision the business needed.

rows.under: Fills every seat with the skill the manager already has. Work that needs a different skill is done badly, or not done.
rows.justRight: Looks at the outcome the team owes, then fills the missing skill with the best person who has it.
rows.over: Gives up a needed skill to hit a mix on paper. The outcome slips, and the team does not call that a hiring miss.

rows.under: Plans the next hires as more people the manager already trusts, which means people like the manager.
rows.justRight: Plans each seat against the outcome. The mix of backgrounds, styles, and skills is whatever makes those jobs succeed.
rows.over: Assigns the next three hires to a quota. Capable people are passed over when they miss the slot, and less capable people are hired when they fill it.

rows.under: Blames the miss on not having enough people who already work the manager's way, and hires more of them.
rows.justRight: Asks which background, style, or skill was missing, and whether the people in the seats could do the work.
rows.over: Hires again to change how the team looks. The result does not improve, because the new person still cannot do the work.
